title: Notifications docs
intro: Notifications sends WhatsApp, email, SMS, browser push, staff push and webhooks for your website, through your own provider keys. Other products send through it with the Notifications server token pasted into their Connections; your own server sends with the same API. Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server.
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https. These pages use your website's real database, keys and providers, so what you send there is sent for real. There is no test mode.
send: Send a message with the server token: POST /v1/messages/<channel> (email, sms, whatsapp, push or staff-push) with the template key, the recipient and the values. The answer (201) is the message as the delivery log keeps it: status sent, queued (waiting for its time), retrying, failed or skipped (unsubscribed, over a send limit, or a product's message you switched off on the channel). Nothing accepted is lost: the message is saved before its first attempt, and an attempt that fails or breaks off (a provider or a database briefly unreachable) answers retrying and is tried again by the retry plan. Send an Idempotency-Key header: the same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer instead of a second message. Send required: true for a message the recipient needs whatever they unsubscribed from (for example an order update from an optional template). Name the values that must never be kept, such as a code or a sign-in link, in secretValues (for example ["code", "link"]): the message is sent with them, and every read of the delivery log (this answer, GET /v1/messages, the delivery-log widget, data-rights exports) shows them hidden (****** or [link hidden]).
templates: Templates live in Notifications: one per template key, channel and language, written in the product dashboard (Settings → Templates) or in the template editor widget. Write {name} where a value goes, and {?name}…{/name} around text that shows only when the value name is not empty (for example {?tracking}Track it: {tracking}{/tracking}); sections may hold other sections of other names. A WhatsApp template with a template name at Meta (providerTemplate) may list buttons, [{ index, type, value }]: index is the button's place in the template at Meta (0–9), type is copy_code or url, and value may hold placeholders, for example {code}. A copy-code button copies its value (it is sent as Meta's authentication templates take it, as a url button whose text is the code); a URL button adds its value to the end of its address. Template keys of other products' own events start with the product id (accounts., ecommerce., chat., payments., growth.) and work while the channel is on; every other key is yours and needs the Merchant send API feature. Your server reads and changes templates with the server token: GET /v1/templates (the templates of switched-on channels), PUT /v1/templates (one template, with the same checks as the dashboard) and DELETE /v1/templates/<key>/<channel>/<language> (default for the default version); each channel's templates need its feature on, and writes count in the settings API's 60 writes per minute. Each change shows in Recent changes with the acting user of the SS-Actor-* headers, else Server. A sensitive template keeps none of its values in the delivery log (they show as ****** or [link hidden]); the templates of Accounts (accounts.…: sign-in codes, magic, reset and setup links) always are, even when saved unchecked. A required message (sign-in codes, order and account updates) is always sent, also to people who unsubscribed by link or keyword (STOP); the templates of Accounts (accounts.…) always are, even when saved unchecked. Any other message is optional and is not sent to people who unsubscribed, unless the send says required: true. Optional templates can use {unsubscribeUrl} (a required template has no unsubscribe link), and only optional emails get one-click unsubscribe headers (an email sent with required: true has none). An urgent message ignores quiet hours; the templates of Accounts (accounts.…) always are, even when saved unchecked.
defaults: Every product ships US-English default templates for the messages it sends (Accounts' sign-in codes, reset, invite and email links; Chat's staff alerts, transcripts and reply alerts; …), so a new website gets them before you write any template. A product's send carries the default words of its message for each channel; Notifications uses them while your website has no template of its own for that key and channel (the recipient's language version, else your default version), and keeps them for the fallback channel. Settings → Templates lists every message your products send, by channel, with its state: Default words, Edited (your version is sent), Switched off, or Not set up. Edit starts from the default words; Reset to default deletes your version, so the default is sent again (versions in other languages stay); Switch off on this channel stops the message there: a send of it is skipped with reason switched_off, shown in the delivery log. Accounts' messages are always sent (switch the sign-in method off in Accounts instead). WhatsApp never has a default: it sends only templates you had approved at Meta. Until you add the WhatsApp template of a product's message with its Meta template name, a send of it on WhatsApp is answered failed with the reason "Not set up: …", kept in the delivery log, and goes to the fallback channel when you set one (for example WhatsApp, then SMS with its default words). Defaults follow the same rules as your templates: the same {placeholders}, optional sections and limits. Your own template keys have no defaults.
retries: Nothing accepted is lost: a message is saved before its first attempt, and an attempt that fails or breaks off (a provider or a database briefly unreachable) counts as a failed attempt. A message that fails is tried again on the same channel, on the next uses of your website after each wait (there are no background jobs, so on a quiet site it waits for the next request). The Retries setting of email, SMS and WhatsApp picks the plan: short (3 attempts: now, then 1 and 5 minutes later; the default) or long (6 attempts: now, then 5 and 15 minutes and 1, 3 and 6 hours later). Push messages use the short plan, and a message keeps the plan it was sent with. Then, with the Fallback channel feature, it is sent once on the fallback channel set in Settings (for example WhatsApp, then SMS) when the recipient has that address and a template exists for it. Every attempt is in the delivery log, in your own database.
timing: Quiet hours hold messages that are not urgent until the end of the quiet window in the recipient's time zone (to.timeZone, else the time zone in business.json). Send limits skip messages over the hourly or daily cap of messages sent to one recipient (Accounts' messages too). Delayed send takes sendAt (ISO-8601); the message goes out on the first use of your website after that time, so it can be late on a quiet site. Messages of Accounts (accounts.…: sign-in codes, magic, reset and setup links) are always urgent and go at once: neither quiet hours nor sendAt hold them, even when their template is saved unchecked; send limits still apply.
languages: With Multi-language templates on, a template can have a version per language. The recipient's language (language, else to.language) picks the version: the exact code, then its base language (pt for pt-BR), else the default version.
providers: Connect a provider per channel in the product dashboard (Connections). Email: SMTP, Resend, SendGrid, Mailgun or Amazon SES. SMS: Twilio, or any SMS gateway with an HTTP API. WhatsApp: Meta WhatsApp Cloud API, Twilio, or any WhatsApp gateway with an HTTP API. A gateway with an HTTP API is sent a POST: give its https address, the body format (json or form), optional headers as a JSON object and a body template, in the field names your gateway asks for. In the headers and the body, {to} is the number with its country code (+447700900123), {toDigits} the same digits without the + (447700900123), {text} the message and {secret} your key; in the body each is encoded for the body format. The gateway's answer says whether it took the message: an HTTP error status, or a JSON answer with error, sent: false, success: false or a status such as failed or rejected, counts as a failed attempt; an id, sid, messageId or message_id in the answer is kept. Example for an imaginary gateway at gateway.example.com that takes JSON and a bearer key: address https://gateway.example.com/v1/messages, json, headers {"Authorization": "Bearer {secret}"}, body {"to": "{to}", "text": "{text}"}. The same gateway with a form and the key in the body: form, body to={toDigits}&message={text}&key={secret}.
keywords: Unsubscribe keywords: point your provider's incoming-message webhook at the address below. Twilio requests are checked with your auth token; the WhatsApp Cloud API with the app secret (and the verify token for its first check). A reply that is one of the keywords in Settings unsubscribes that number from optional messages.
push: Browser push: create a P-256 key pair (VAPID, for example with npx web-push generate-vapid-keys) and enter it in Connections → Push keys. Copy the service worker below to the root of your website as /ss-notifications-sw.js, then place the push-permission widget. When a visitor turns notifications on, the widget fires the ss-notifications:subscribed event on window with { subscriberId } and keeps it in localStorage; send it to your server and link it to your user, then send with to: { subscriberId }. Staff push works the same way in your admin with a ticket (permission push.subscribe); send with to: { staffId } (the user id in the ticket).
webhooks: Outgoing webhooks: add up to 5 https URLs in Settings → Webhook URLs, each with the events it takes (none: every event), and a random signing secret (at least 24 characters) in Connections. Your server reads and saves the same list with the server token: GET /v1/lists/webhook_urls and PUT /v1/lists/webhook_urls with { value: [{ url, events }] }, where events lists full types such as message.failed or payments.payment.paid. Each event is a POST of JSON { id, type, createdAt, websiteId, data } with the header SS-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">. Check it before trusting the body, and refuse times older than 5 minutes. Each delivery is tried up to 5 times in all (again after 1, 5 and 30 minutes and 2 hours), on later uses of your website.
events: Other products' events: with the Notifications server token pasted into their Connections, every product that publishes events (for example payments.payment.paid) forwards each one right after it happens to POST /v1/events with { id, type, at, data } and the event id as its Idempotency-Key. Those events go to the webhook URLs that take their type (or take every event), signed the same way; the Events setting picks among Notifications' own events only. The webhook keeps the product's event id as id and its time as createdAt, so your server can match it with that product's GET /v1/events. id (evt_…) and at (ISO-8601) are optional: without them the webhook gets a new id and the time it was received.
log: The delivery log is kept in your own database: forever by default (0), or for the days set in Settings → Delivery log (delivery_log.retentionDays, 1–3650; your database's expiry index removes messages and webhook events that many days after they are sent, failed or skipped, and waiting ones stay). A change applies to messages finished from then on. It never keeps a secret: the values of sensitive templates and those named in secretValues are hidden in its words, values, WhatsApp parameters and buttons, also in data-rights exports. The real words are kept sealed with ENCRYPTION_KEY only while the message still has attempts to make, then cleared; a waiting message whose sealed words no longer open (ENCRYPTION_KEY changed without ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS) fails. Your server reads it with GET /v1/messages?status=&channel=&to=&cursor=&limit= (newest first) and GET /v1/messages/<id>, and counts it with the same filters: GET /v1/messages/count → { count, capped } and GET /v1/messages/counts?by=status|channel|template|source → { total, groups } (a one-off message from your staff counts under template none). The delivery-log widget reads the same with a ticket (log.read) under /v1/admin/messages.
install: Add the script to the pages of your website and place the visitor widget where it should appear. Widgets render nothing while their feature is off or the product is stopped.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket: the delivery log (log.read), the template editor (templates.edit), send a message (messages.send) and staff notifications (push.subscribe). Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features.
business: Every product reads your business basics from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain and the time zone is UTC.
api: Routes answer JSON (204 has no body); errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code. The reference below says what every call takes and answers. Lists are paged with cursor and limit. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off.
